lifecycle.description: Kept running, with no new features and no new users

lifecycle.label: Phase-out
lifecycle.description: Being retired; its users are moving elsewhere

lifecycle.label: Archived
lifecycle.description: Switched off, with its data kept as policy requires

sourcing.label: Software as a service
sourcing.description: Run by a vendor and used over the internet

sourcing.label: Commercial, run here

sourcing.description: Written and kept by the organization's own people

sourcing.label: Open source, run here
sourcing.description: Open-source software run on our own hosting

sourcing.label: Low-code

purpose.label: Mission
purpose.description: Sets the organization apart, or is how its mission is done

purpose.label: Operations
purpose.description: Carries out the day-to-day work and its transactions

purpose.label: Foundation
purpose.description: A shared platform other applications rest on

pace.label: Steady
pace.description: Expected to change slowly and last many years

pace.label: Evolving
pace.description: Expected to change often as needs change

pace.label: Experimental
pace.description: New or exploratory; expected to change or end soon

tiers.description: Care, safety, or the organization's core work stops without it

tiers.label: 2 · Business critical
tiers.description: Important work stops within a day without it

tiers.label: 3 · Business operational
tiers.description: Its loss would be felt within days and worked around

tiers.label: 4 · Administrative
tiers.description: Could be done without for weeks with little effect

tiers.label: 5 · Minimal
tiers.description: Could be switched off with almost no effect

sign_in.label: Single sign-on with multi-factor
sign_in.description: Organization sign-in and a second factor

sign_in.label: Its own accounts, with multi-factor
sign_in.description: Separate accounts, with a second factor

sign_in.label: Shared accounts
sign_in.description: Accounts or passwords shared between people

sign_in.label: No sign-in
sign_in.description: Open to anyone who can reach it

monitoring.label: None
monitoring.description: Nobody would know it was down until someone said so

monitoring.label: Metrics and logs
monitoring.description: Its health is measured and its logs are kept

monitoring.label: Alerting
monitoring.description: Problems raise an alert to someone

monitoring.label: Alerting to on-call
monitoring.description: Problems reach a staffed on-call rota

backup.label: Unverified
backup.description: Backed up, but a restore has not been tested

backup.label: Tested
backup.description: Backed up, and a restore has been tested

backup.label: Vendor managed
backup.description: The vendor backs it up under its agreement

data_classes.label: Public
data_classes.description: May be shared with anyone: published results, public web content.

data_classes.label: Internal
data_classes.description: Meant for the organization's own work: plans, procedures, most email.

data_classes.label: Personal information
data_classes.description: About identifiable staff, students, donors, or the public.

data_classes.label: De-identified research data
data_classes.description: Research data from which participants cannot reasonably be identified.

data_classes.label: Identifiable research data
data_classes.description: Research data about participants who can be identified.

data_classes.label: Protected health information
data_classes.description: Health information about identifiable patients, held under health privacy law.

data_classes.label: Controlled-access data
data_classes.description: Data received under an agreement that limits who may see it and how.

data_classes.label: Payment card data
data_classes.description: Card numbers and related data, held under the card industry's rules.

radar.label: Hold
radar.description: Not for new work; move away when you can

application_roles.label: Accountable owner
application_roles.description: Answers for it and its record; there is one

application_roles.label: Business owner
application_roles.description: Speaks for the people who use it

application_roles.label: Technical owner
application_roles.description: Answers for how it is built and run

application_roles.label: Support contact
application_roles.description: Whom to call when it is not working

application_roles.label: Data steward
application_roles.description: Answers for the data it holds

external_systems.label: Configuration item
external_systems.description: Its record in the infrastructure inventory

external_systems.label: Sign-in registration
external_systems.description: Its registration with the identity provider

external_systems.label: Contract number
external_systems.description: As the purchasing system knows it

external_systems.label: Governance record
external_systems.description: Its record in another governance system

environments.label: Production
environments.description: What people use for real work

environments.label: Staging
environments.description: A copy of production for trying a change before it goes live

environments.label: Test
environments.description: For testing; holds no real data

environments.label: Disaster recovery
environments.description: A standby to fail over to

platform_kinds.label: Data center
platform_kinds.description: Servers the organization runs in its own or a leased room

platform_kinds.label: Cloud account
platform_kinds.description: An account or subscription with a cloud provider

platform_kinds.label: Compute cluster
platform_kinds.description: A shared cluster, such as research computing

platform_kinds.label: Hosting provider
platform_kinds.description: Servers or platforms a provider runs for the organization

platform_kinds.label: A vendor's service
platform_kinds.description: The vendor runs it; the organization only uses it

platform_kinds.label: People's own computers
platform_kinds.description: Installed on desktops, laptops, or instruments

cost_categories.label: License or subscription
cost_categories.description: What is paid for the right to use it

cost_categories.label: Hosting
cost_categories.description: Servers, cloud, storage, and network it runs on

cost_categories.label: Support contract
cost_categories.description: Vendor support, maintenance, and managed services

cost_categories.label: Our own people's time
cost_categories.description: The effort of those who run and change it, as money

agreement_states.label: In place
agreement_states.description: An agreement covers the data the vendor handles

agreement_states.label: Not needed
agreement_states.description: The vendor handles no data that needs one

agreement_states.label: Missing
agreement_states.description: One is needed and there is none

interface_methods.label: API call
interface_methods.description: One application calls the other as it needs to

interface_methods.label: File transfer
interface_methods.description: Files are sent or collected on a schedule

interface_methods.label: Scheduled extract and load
interface_methods.description: A job copies data from one database to another

interface_methods.label: Shared database
interface_methods.description: One reads or writes the other's database directly

interface_methods.label: Messages or events
interface_methods.description: A queue, a stream, or an integration engine carries messages

interface_methods.label: Embedded page or hand-off
interface_methods.description: One shows the other's pages, or hands the user across

interface_methods.label: By hand
interface_methods.description: Someone exports from one and uploads or re-keys into the other

dispositions.label: Maintain
dispositions.description: Keep it as it is, run efficiently

dispositions.label: Tolerate
dispositions.description: Keep it at the least cost, and look again

dispositions.label: Modernize
dispositions.description: Valuable, but technically weak: upgrade, re-platform, or refactor

dispositions.label: Replace
dispositions.description: The function is needed; this asset should go

dispositions.label: Consolidate
dispositions.description: Does what another application does; move its users there

dispositions.label: Retire
dispositions.description: Little value; retire without a successor

dispositions.label: Incubate
dispositions.description: New or experimental; not yet judged on use

dispositions.label: Assess
dispositions.description: Not enough is known to recommend

fields.label: Ethics protocols
fields.help: The ethics review protocol numbers of the studies that depend on it.

fields.label: Data management plan
fields.help: Where the plan for the data it holds is kept.

fields.label: Accessibility
fields.help: How well people with disabilities can use it, as last checked.

definition.text: An application is software, or a service built from software, that people name, use for a purpose, and could decide to keep, change, or retire as one thing.
examples: A lab's sample tracker, used by three labs
not_examples: A server or a database on its own: record it as a component of what it serves
A report or a module of a larger system: a component of that system
A spreadsheet one person keeps for themselves
A programming language or a platform: a technology

questions.text: How closely does it support what the organization is trying to achieve?
questions.help: Think of the organization's plans and priorities, not only the unit's.
levels: It works against our direction, or nobody can say what it is for
It supports work we are moving away from
It supports routine work, not our priorities
It supports one of our stated priorities
It is central to how we will reach our priorities

questions.text: How well does it do what its users need today?
questions.help: Ask the people who use it, if you are not one of them.
levels: It does not do what people need; they work around it
It does some of what is needed, with many workarounds
It does most of what is needed, with some workarounds
It does what is needed, with few complaints
It does what is needed well, and people would choose it

questions.text: Will the organization still need what it does in three years?
questions.help: The need, not this particular application.
levels: No: the need is ending
Probably not
Probably, but it may change a lot
Yes, much as it is today
Yes, and the need is growing

questions.text: How well does it meet the service its users expect?
questions.help: Outages, slowness, errors, and lost work over the last year.
levels: It fails often, or for long periods
It fails several times a year and people notice
It fails now and then; people cope
It rarely fails, and recovers quickly
It meets every expectation; failures are very rare and short

questions.text: How easy is it to change, upgrade, and keep current?
questions.help: For something bought: how easy it is to upgrade and configure.
levels: Changes are avoided because they break things; nobody fully understands it
Changes are slow and risky; little documentation or testing
Changes are routine but manual; some documentation
Changes are routine and mostly tested; documented
Changes are safe and frequent: automated tests, deployment, and current documentation

questions.text: How confident are we in the vendor and the product's future?
questions.help: Their support, their roadmap, and whether they will be around.
levels: The product is ending, or the vendor is failing
Support is poor, or the product is no longer developed
Adequate support; an uncertain future
Good support and an active product
A strong vendor and a product with a clear future

questions.text: How much effort does it take to keep running?
questions.help: Fixing, administering, helping users: the people's time, not money.
levels: A constant drain: it needs attention most days
Heavy: regular firefighting
Moderate: routine care each month
Light: occasional attention
Very light: it looks after itself

questions.text: How much effort does it take to change or upgrade?
questions.help: A typical enhancement or a version upgrade.
levels: Each change is a project of months
Changes take weeks and are often late
Changes take days to weeks
Changes take days, and estimates hold
Changes take hours to days

questions.text: Are there known gaps against the rules that apply to it?
questions.help: Open audit findings, a missing agreement with a vendor, an overdue review.
levels: Serious known gaps, with nobody working on them
Serious known gaps being worked on
Minor known gaps
No known gaps, but it has not been reviewed recently
No known gaps, and it was reviewed recently

dimensions.label: Business value
dimensions.help: How much the organization would lose without it.

dimensions.label: Technical health
dimensions.help: How well it is built, run, and kept current.

dimensions.label: Cost and burden
dimensions.help: What it takes to keep. 5 means a light burden.

dimensions.label: Risk exposure
dimensions.help: What could go wrong while it is kept. 5 means little exposure.

cost_burden.label: Cost per user
cost_burden.unit: a year for each person who uses it

cost_burden.label: License use
cost_burden.unit: percent of the licenses bought are in use

business_value.reason: It is a system of record for regulated information

guardrails.label: Protected from retirement
guardrails.reason: It is mission or business critical, the only provider of a capability, or a system of record for regulated information, so it needs a successor.

flags.text: Its grant ends within a year, with no decision this year
Confidential or restricted data under a contract with no data agreement
A contract's notice date is within 90 days
Its data must be archived before it goes
Its decision is due for review
